No sed runs here, so there is no GNU/BSD portability defect to fix. The L1b linter shipped with this fix exempts the same line via its quoted-test-data post-filter.
review_reason: Traced end to end: line 539 is an element of the RDENY25 array (declared :527, closed :564, each entry shaped '<command>:::<mutant-ids>'). The consumer at :590-592 splits off the command text and hands it to rh_run (:498-500), which wraps it with JSON.stringify into tool_input.command and pipes it to the hook's STDIN. The hook (.claude/hooks/xprov-deny-allowlist-approve.sh:38 -> xprov-bash-class.cjs) only reads and pattern-matches the text; neither file holds an execution primitive (no eval, exec, spawnSync, child_process). Nothing runs, so there is no GNU/BSD portability defect. Rewriting it to sed -i.bak would also move the M5 coverage point: xprov-bash-class.cjs:61 treats only 'sed -n <range>p' as read-only, and M5 exists to prove a writing sed is denied. Verified independently of the L1b linter, whose own exemption was found too coarse in the same review and hardened in ced38e8.
